question: Should OpenClaw accept Linux headless node-host `system.notify`, and if so which backend contract should the first implementation support?
rationale: The source gap is clear and the exact command is core-reserved, but backend dependencies, D-Bus or dunst scope, headless-session behavior, and invocation security need maintainer intent before automation changes runtime behavior.

options.title: Approve focused notify-send support
options.body: Add a narrow core node-host implementation for desktop sessions using `notify-send`, safe argv invocation, structured unavailable results, docs, tests, and live Linux proof; defer D-Bus and dunst-specific behavior.

options.title: Broaden backend support now
options.body: Define and implement a larger backend matrix such as `notify-send`, D-Bus, and dunst-specific behavior, accepting the extra support and validation surface up front.

options.title: Defer to Linux companion direction
options.body: Keep this issue open behind the broader Linux companion app plan and do not add headless node-host notifications until that product surface is settled.

recommendation.title: Approve focused notify-send support
recommendation.body: Add a narrow core node-host implementation for desktop sessions using `notify-send`, safe argv invocation, structured unavailable results, docs, tests, and live Linux proof; defer D-Bus and dunst-specific behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The current visible history and prior review context route the core node-host command boundary through this owner path.
